name: Cinderblock Nightwatch Wrap Set
description: Built for low-visibility, low-movement work — the kind of watching that happens in doorways and on broken catwalks at 03:00. The foundation is a thermal long-sleeve base in charcoal heather, heavily pilled from repeated washing in whatever water is available, the neck stretched wide and re-hemmed with a doubled strip of elastic salvaged from a Pragma Systems base layer. Over this is a structured wrap-jacket in a deep, muted rust-brown — originally a single-piece garment, now split at the left side seam and re-closed with a row of mismatched pressure snaps that allow rapid removal or ventilation adjustment. The wrap folds across the chest and ties with a wide obi-style sash in faded indigo, its ends frayed to loose threads that the wearer has stopped cutting. The sash carries two flat pockets stitched directly onto it — one holding a folded emergency mylar sheet, one with a broken-seam closure holding a small medkit. The lower half is loose trousers in near-black canvas, hem-gathered at the ankle with salvaged elastic so they don't snag on debris, the left thigh bearing a large iron-on acid-shield patch in matte gray. Footwear is a low boot in cracked synthetic suede, the toe cap reinforced with a strip of steel salvaged from a junction box cover, riveted in place with hardware-store bolts. The head covering is a wide, flat-crown wrap cap in washed linen the color of old concrete, its brim stiffened with a strip of reclaimed wire sewn into the hem. The whole palette — rust, indigo shadow, charcoal, near-black — is dark enough to disappear in Shelf shadows but not so uniform as to read as tactical.
functionality: Wrap-jacket with snap-release side for rapid removal; sash-mounted flat pockets; ankle-gathered trousers prevent debris snagging; reinforced steel toe cap; wire-stiffened brim cap for weather and concealment; muted palette for low-visibility work
what_it_says: This is community infrastructure clothing — the person who wears this is probably keeping watch over something or someone. The obi sash signals a hand-craft tradition maintained even under Shelf conditions, a quiet insistence on form. The mismatched snaps and frayed threads say the form comes second to function, but not by much. There's dignity here, worn thin but intact.
worn_by: runners who move between Shelf districts after dark
elders who remember when the obi meant something specific
manufacturer: Self-assembled; wrap fabric sourced from a collapsed textile market stall; sash is repurposed Tier 2 import fabric
price_range: Φ 18–40 complete; Φ 5–12 for sash alone on secondary market
story_hooks: The indigo sash is cut from a garment that belonged to someone who didn't survive the last major Shelf flooding — the wearer knows this and so does anyone from that neighborhood who sees it.
The flat pocket on the sash contains something besides a medkit: a folded document, handwritten, that someone paid to have delivered and the wearer hasn't decided whether to deliver it yet.

A TESSERA field agent doing gene-mod compliance sweeps stops the wearer specifically because the ankle-gathered trousers are a known style marker for people running unlicensed geneware underground — it's a profiling assumption, and it may or may not be correct.
related_entities: Ringo Corponation SlipThread MX-3 Urban Cable Micro-Mobility Rig

physical_description.visual_profile: A layered, deliberately mismatched silhouette designed for invisibility in urban shadows. The outfit reads as DIY-assembled fieldwork wear — functional, patched, and built for rapid adjustment. On the body, it creates a soft, rumpled column that absorbs light rather than reflects it. The wide wrap-jacket and loosely-tied sash give an almost robe-like drape despite the structured interior. The wide-brimmed cap and wrapped ankle cuffs add a deliberate shapelessness that obscures the wearer's exact form. Overall impression: a figure built to blend into doorways, catwalks, and the liminal spaces between infrastructure.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and intentionally oversized in the torso; the wrap-jacket drapes rather than clings, with the split side seam allowing ventilation or rapid removal. The sash ties loose and long, its frayed ends reaching mid-thigh. Trousers are straight-cut and deliberately un-tailored, gathered at the ankle to prevent snagging. The cap sits low and wide, obscuring the upper face. The overall fit prioritizes movement freedom and the ability to divest layers quickly — nothing binds or restricts.
physical_description.primary_material: Thermal base in synthetic knit; wrap-jacket in salvaged dense cotton or linen blend; obi sash in faded linen-cotton; trousers in scavenged canvas; cap in washed linen; boots in cracked synthetic suede with steel-plate toe reinforce
physical_description.texture: Heavily pilled and worn — the base layer shows repeated washing damage. The wrap-jacket is soft but carries visible creases and stress marks from re-seaming. The sash is frayed at the edges with loose threads left deliberately uncut. Canvas trousers have a stiff, broken-in quality. The cap fabric is soft and sun-faded, with visible wire reinforcement through the brim creating subtle ridges. Boots show deep cracking in the synthetic suede, with raw steel peeking through at the toe. The iron-on patch on the left thigh is matte and slightly peeling at the corners.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep, muted palette: charcoal heather base layer, rust-brown wrap-jacket, faded indigo sash, near-black canvas trousers, old-concrete gray cap, cracked synthetic suede boots. The matte gray acid-shield patch provides minimal contrast. All colors are desaturated and weathered — nothing bright or reflective. The overall effect is a grayscale-plus-rust aesthetic.
physical_description.closures: Mismatched pressure snaps running down the left side seam of the wrap-jacket (allowing rapid opening/closing). The sash ties with a traditional knot at the side. Elastic-gathered ankle cuffs on trousers (friction-fit, no hardware). The cap has no visible closure. Pockets on the sash are stitched-closed; one is broken-seamed.
distinctive_features: Pressure snaps down the left side seam of wrap-jacket — deliberately mismatched, allowing rapid ventilation or full removal
Re-hemmed neckline with doubled elastic strip salvaged from Pragma Systems base layer
Two flat pockets stitched directly onto the obi sash — one containing emergency mylar sheet, one with broken-seam medkit closure
Large matte gray iron-on acid-shield patch on left thigh, partially peeling
Steel-reinforced toe cap on boots, riveted with hardware-store bolts
Wire reinforcement sewn into cap brim
Frayed sash ends left deliberately uncut
Elastic-gathered ankle cuffs to prevent debris snagging
Visible re-seaming and pilling throughout — no attempt at repair concealment
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 (sub-grade/ungoverned). Every component is salvaged, repurposed, or assembled from scrap. The 'Tier 2 import fabric' in the sash suggests a single high-end material element incorporated into otherwise entirely sub-grade construction. This is not luxury slumming — this is the actual uniform of the resource-scavenged.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street security, informal night-watch, urban salvage crew, or ungoverned sector infrastructure monitor. The outfit signals someone who works in darkness, in places where visibility is a liability, and who needs to disappear quickly or adjust on the fly. There is no brand signaling; the only manufactured item is the acid-shield patch (industrial safety wear repurposed as fashion). Wearing this says: *I am invisible by design, equipped for the work that happens in the gaps, and I own every repair on my body.*
physical_description.condition_typical: Heavily worn and patched. Not dirty, but weathered beyond the point of normal care. The pilling is extensive and left unaddressed. Visible creases from repeated folding. The synthetic suede of the boots shows deep cracking. The sash fraying is deliberate abandonment of repair. The pressure snaps are mismatched because replacement wasn't a priority. This is an outfit that has absorbed the work it was built for and makes no apology for it.
